data.title: Streaming Response
data.tagline: A response sent and displayed in consecutive pieces as it is generated
data.learningOutcome: You can distinguish a fast first piece from the total time to finish an answer.
data.description: A chat answer can appear as if it is typing. An early first piece makes waiting feel shorter, but the full answer can still take time to generate and transmit.

learning.assumes: You have watched a chat answer appear word by word or in pieces.
learning.outcome: You can distinguish a fast first piece from the total time to finish an answer.

explanation.title: Pieces arrive
explanation.text: The server sends text or status events; one piece may not be a complete word.

explanation.title: The interface appends them
explanation.text: The product adds each text piece in order to the existing content.

explanation.title: Generation continues
explanation.text: Early content reduces perceived waiting, but total time still depends on the rest.

data.boundary: Streaming makes content visible sooner; it does not automatically make the model finish the whole response faster.

lessonPractice.title: A long answer takes 20 seconds, and the product wants earlier visible content while handling failure and completion correctly. How should it work?

options.label: Render a real stream incrementally with generating, complete, interrupted, and retry states
options.feedback: Streaming reduces time to first content, while explicit states keep interrupted output from looking final.

options.label: Wait for the complete answer, then reveal it slowly with a typewriter animation
options.feedback: Users still wait for full generation and then receive an artificial delay rather than earlier content.

options.label: Mark the task complete at the first character and append later content in the background
options.feedback: First content is not completion, and premature state breaks copying, saving, and error handling.

data.agentPrompt: Use the real response stream to update one message incrementally and distinguish connecting, generating, complete, interrupted, and retry states. First content is not completion; preserve partial output on interruption and allow stop.
